CONDEMNED. Kept as evidence, not as a schema.

This was the library's default before the rewrite, and the reason the default was emptied. Measured on 80 real APIGen-MT retail conversations -- real customer-service traffic with real tool calls -- it extracted 46 facts, and every one read in context was wrong. Fourteen of fourteen, judged by reading the registering turn:

  destination_address = "perfectly suit my needs"
  destination_address = "for any price difference"
  destination_address = "my existing PayPal account"
  destination_address = "the Visa card ending in 2364"

The `use` trigger is the culprit: in a retail conversation "use" is almost always about money. The original 60-transcript coding sample produced three examples of the same failure; this is the same defect at scale, on data that is actually the domain the schema was written for.

Do not copy these patterns. The measured replacement is contextgc/schemas/logistics.json.

destination_address: (?:deliver to|bring it to|change (?:the )?(?:address|destination) to|my address is|come to|new address:?|confirmed as|destination is|actually (?:use|send (?:it|them) to)|reroute (?:the rider )?to|use)\s+([A-Za-z0-9\s,–#-]{4,40}?)(?:\.|\,|$|\bwith\b|\band\b|\bplease\b|\bfor\b)
